text:
lina_pm: Quick sync — proposing a new paid add-on: Predictable Throughput Add-on (PTA). Goal: give mid-market customers a per-route reserved throughput pool + 99th pct latency SLA for critical endpoints. Thinking this sits above Pro tier as an add-on. Thoughts on pricing, launch gating, and contract constraints?

miguel_eng: short take — technically feasible. We'll need: per-route tokens, headroom for autoscale, and a fallback plan to best-effort if capacity exhausted.

chloe_sales: Customers asked for something like this (two pilots last quarter). They want a simple SKU and a clear cost/benefit in $/RPS. Complex terms kill deals.

sam_ops: ops concerns: 1) monitoring per-tenant per-route usage, 2) burst isolation to avoid noisy neighbors, 3) playbook for when reserved pool is exhausted. Also need per-tenant quotas surfaced to console.

lina_pm: Agree re simplicity. Draft launch gating criteria proposal: 
- 2 pilot customers signed (min $X/month)
- SLO test: 99p latency validated under 2x reserved load in staging
- Console: per-route reservation UI + alerts
- Billing: itemized add-on line in invoice

miguel_eng: Technical checklist for engineering: 
```
- API: POST /reservations {route, rps, duration, priority}
- Runtime: enforce token bucket per route + KV cache awareness
- Fallback: configurable policy (queue, degrade, route-to-best-effort)
- Metrics: reserved_rps, consumed_rps, dropped_rps
```
Will need ~6 sprints to build MVP with a small cross-team effort.

chloe_sales: Pricing suggestion from field: either flat monthly band (e.g., up to 200 rps = $Y/mo, 201-1000 = $Z/mo) or a blended $/reserved-rps that discounts with scale. Preference: banded SKU for clarity.

dave_finance: banded SKU is easier to forecast. Need to model cost: expected utilization, marginal GPU hours for reserved capacity, and effective uplift. Can you drop a conservative margin target? 40%+ on top of infra cost would be healthy.

anya_legal: Contract asks: must be explicit about what "reserved" means (soft reservation vs hard guarantee), remedies for breach of SLA, and data-exposure implications if we route to fallback models. Also include migration path off PTA and termination triggers.

sam_ops: For breach handling: prefer automated fallback plus customer credit table by severity. Avoid open-ended liability.

lina_pm: Proposed SLA wording (draft): "We guarantee 99th percentile latency for requests served from the reserved pool during normal operation. In the event we cannot meet this due to infrastructure failure, we will notify and provide service credits as described in Sec. X." OK to iterate with legal.

anya_legal: Fine as a start. We need to define "normal operation" and list exclusions (force majeure, customer misconfiguration, DDoS). Also add max credit cap per month.

chloe_sales: For pilots, can we offer an onboarding discount and a one-time migration assist? That helps adoption.

lina_pm: Agreed. Pilot package: 25% off first 3 months + shared runbook + one onboarding migration day from SE. Launch decision: ship to GA after 2 pilots + SLO pass + billing + legal terms finalized.

miguel_eng: ETA note: MVP perf + metrics + fallback = ~6 sprints, but we can do a lean pilot feature (console + billing + naive reservation in front-of-runtime) in ~10 weeks if we prioritize.

dave_finance: I'll run a quick P&L for the banded SKU and share numbers by EOD Friday.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging PTA-reservation-service deployed to cluster-pt-3 at 2025-02-05T15:34Z :rocket:

lina_pm: Next steps: Miguel to scope engineering epic with estimated tickets, Dave to provide pricing band model, Anya to draft SLA bullets, Chloe to shortlist pilot customers. Check back next Tues 10am PT. :calendar:

chloe_sales: Adding @acme-ent and @fintech-beta to pilot outreach this afternoon.

sam_ops: I'll start a runbook template and tester for exhaustion scenarios.

lina_pm: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the sticky record. If anyone has objections to the launch gating criteria DM me. :thumbsup:
